actual_findings: Deputy Foreign Minister Professor Phiri treated the 1989 Delimitation Treaty as the governing agreed boundary; prospective dialogue concerned funding, sensitisation and physical demarcation between lakes Mweru and Tanganyika.

Minister stated Zambia had received no Congolese query or correspondence questioning validity of that treaty/border as of this 2009 answer. This is a dated ministerial statement, not independent proof of every later position.
The answer refers to a February2004 point of order and subsequent Lands Minister statement describing the treaty boundary. It gives no exact statement day, catalogue identifier or attachment.

Full retrieved page contains no PDF/download/attachment href; the relevant section does not supply a signed treaty scan, maps I/II, registration number, gazette issue or institutional custody reference.
An MP challenged the agreement and rights implications; this question is not substituted for the government answer or treated as current spatial adjudication.
